newsitem.title: USA: Russia, Kyrgyzstan won't lift diplomats' immunity.
newsitem.headline: Russia, Kyrgyzstan won't lift diplomats' immunity.

text.p: Russia and Kyrgyzstan have refused to waive the immunity of diplomats cited for drunk driving in the Washington area, so the State Department said Wednesday it would bar both men from driving for a year.

Spokesman Nicholas Burns said the department received a letter from the Russian embassy on May 9 saying immunity would not be waived for second secretary Vadim Savelyev, cited for drunk driving by Maryland police near Annapolis on March 30.

Burns told reporters the Kyrgyz embassy had also said it would not waive the immunity of second secretary Erkinbek Atabekov, who was cited for drunk driving after colliding with two parked cars in Washington on April 10.

As a result of the decisions, the State Department, which issues foreign diplomats with drivers' licenses, would suspend them for a year, preventing the two men from driving in the United States, Burns said.

In a third case involving Olesy Yarotskiy, wife of Ukrainian second secretary Vadym Yarotskiy, the State Department was still awaiting reports from District of Columbia authorities and had so far taken no action, he said.
Yarotskiy failed a breathalyser test following a collision in Washington on April 12.
No one was hurt in any of the three incidents.

In the most serious case this year involving diplomats from the former Soviet Union, a car driven by Georgian official Georgui Makharadze was involved in a five-car crash in Washington in January that killed a teenage girl.
Georgian President Eduard Shevardnadze waived Makharadze's immunity and he is due to stand stand trial in July on involuntary homicide and other charges.
